newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Unsecured Kiwi creditors to get nothing - liquidator.
newsitem.headline: Unsecured Kiwi creditors to get nothing - liquidator.

text.p: The liquidators of collapsed Kiwi International Airlines said on Friday it was "most unlikely" that unsecured creditors would recover anything.
Colin McCloy of Price Waterhouse said there was no certainty of preferential creditors recovering anything.

"The liquidators estimate that at August 26, 1996 amounts due to the public in respect of prepaid but unutilised airline tickets were in the region of NZ$5 million. Amounts due to trade and other creditors at the date of liquidation are estimated to exceed $3 million," the liquidators said.
Hamilton-based Kiwi went into liquidation on September 10.
